title: Khaemenes Mathematics Continuum
description: Shared public mathematics information contract spanning early learning through research-level mathematics. Courses own curriculum; this file supplies common progression, evidence, tool, and bounded Mini-Cloud definitions.

authority.courseOwnershipRule: Each course remains authoritative for its own lessons, assessments, sequence, and local learning records.
authority.dependencyRule: Courses may read this continuum for shared mathematics metadata but must fail gracefully if the file is unavailable.
authority.archiveRule: Historical snapshots are preserved in ARSHIF and are never used as the live runtime dependency.

stages.label: Pre-K / Creche
stages.proofStandard: No formal proof. Learners explain observations with words, objects, movement, drawings, or patterns.

stages.label: Kinder Garden
stages.proofStandard: Reasoning is concrete and visual; explanations matter more than symbolic formality.

stages.label: Elementary Mathematics
stages.proofStandard: Students justify strategies and properties with examples, diagrams, equations, and counterexamples appropriate to grade level.

stages.label: Middle School Mathematics
stages.proofStandard: Students move from examples toward generalized arguments and distinguish a convincing pattern from a justified conclusion.

stages.label: High School Mathematics
stages.proofStandard: Formal and semi-formal proof are required where appropriate. Computation, graphing, simulation, and measurement support reasoning but do not automatically constitute proof.

stages.label: Higher Learning Mathematics
stages.proofStandard: Theorem use, proof, computation, visualization, experiment, and citation must be labeled distinctly. Objective scores cannot substitute for required written mathematical evidence.

stages.label: Advanced / Research Mathematics
stages.proofStandard: Claims must carry explicit mathematical status. Computational or visual evidence may motivate, test, or falsify claims but does not certify a theorem without a valid proof or cited theorem.

evidencePrinciples: A numerical score measures only what the scored instrument actually assessed.
Proof evidence remains distinct from objective-question performance.
A visualization can reveal structure or suggest a claim without proving it.
A computation can support, test, reproduce, or refute a claim without automatically proving the general case.
A cited theorem requires a recorded source when citation evidence is part of the task.
Learner reasoning should remain visible; mentor support must not erase the learner's mathematical voice.
Tools should expose uncertainty, assumptions, units, domains, and limitations where relevant.

neverClaims: formal proof solely from a drawing

publicTools.title: Evidence & Citation Studio
neverClaims: source truth merely because a claim is stored
proof merely because a source states a result

miniClouds.label: Mathematics Context Cloud
miniClouds.purpose: Expose the learner's current mathematical stage, course, lesson, objectives, prerequisite concepts, pathway, and evidence requirements in a compact public-safe context object.

miniClouds.label: Mathematics Tool Cloud
miniClouds.purpose: Match approved public mathematics tools to lesson needs by stage, strand, evidence mode, and accessibility.
may: recommend calculator, CAD, geometry, or other approved public resources
mustNot: treat tool output as proof by default

miniClouds.label: Mathematics Evidence Cloud
miniClouds.purpose: Keep score, reasoning, proof, computation, citation, and reflection statuses distinct.
mustNot: merge objective scores with proof status

miniClouds.label: Mathematics Lab Cloud
miniClouds.purpose: Package constructions, measurements, simulations, computations, annotations, and reproducibility notes for review.
mustNot: equate visual agreement with mathematical proof

miniClouds.label: Mathematics Research Cloud
miniClouds.purpose: Support source-aware theorem use, provenance, conjecture testing, counterexample search, and reproducible scholarly work.
may: separate cited results from derived work
mustNot: treat AI output as a source

miniClouds.label: Mathematics Continuity Cloud
miniClouds.purpose: Carry public-safe learner progress references across grade bands without changing the authority of school-specific records.

courseContract.canonicalCourseIdRule: A course has one permanent courseId across lessons, assessments, exports, labs, evidence records, and resource routing.
courseContract.gracefulFallback: If this continuum cannot be loaded, the course must continue with its local curriculum and local-safe defaults.
